names.form: Filofteia de la Curtea de Argeș
names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 7 decembrie, «Sfânta Muceniță Filofteia de la Curtea de Argeș», with the rank word left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 28 Μαΐου, «Οσία Φιλοθέα η Παρθενομάρτυρας», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru’s line for 7 декабря ст. ст., «Филофея Румынская, мц.», with the rank word left off. The calendar gives her the country and not the city: the folder's Romanian form is «Filofteia de la Curtea de Argeș», where her relics lie. The line on the day page itself gives the name in the genitive.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 7 декабря ст. ст. — «Мц. Филофеи (1060) (Рум.).»

attestations.note: The same woman and the same menologion day the Romanian row already keeps. The calendar's own «(Рум.)» marks the entry as a Romanian saint, and its name link reads «Филофея Румынская, мц.», Philothea the Romanian, martyr — «мц.» is the `martyr` this folder already holds, and `types` are untouched. No life page stands behind the line: the line and the name link are all there is here.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 7 decembrie — «Sfânta Muceniță Filofteia de la Curtea de Argeș»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 28ης Μαΐου — «Οσία Φιλοθέα η Παρθενομάρτυρας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 28 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», which is not the folder's Romanian day of 7 December, and the two calendars keep her on two days. It is plainly the same woman: the page follows her relics from Eastern Thrace to Tarnovo under Kaloyan, on to Vidin in 1395, and then says that after the fall of Vidin in 1396 their traces were lost for a long time and «τα ανακαλύπτουμε με βεβαιότητα στο δεύτερο ήμισυ του 16ου αιώνος μ.Χ. στην πόλη Άρτζες της Ουγγροβλαχίας» — we find them with certainty in the second half of the sixteenth century in the town of Argeș in Ungro-Wallachia, which is this folder's own place. One attestation row per church is the schema, so the Greek row records the 28 Μαΐου day page quoted here and the Romanian 7 December stays where it is. saint.gr places her birth at Molyvoto in Pamphylia in Asia Minor, names her parents as the patrician John and Irene, and gives her age at marriage as fourteen and her husband as Constantine — none of which is added to the folder's dates, since the page gives no year at all for her life. It prints no hymn.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (25 September 2026).

hymns.text: Întru răbdarea ta ţi-ai agonisit plata ta, Fericită Filofteia, întru ispite neîncetat răbdând, bătăi suferind, în necazuri binevoind, pe săraci miluindu-i şi pe flămânzi săturându-i; roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu, bună fecioară, să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfintei Mucenițe Filofteia de la Curtea de Argeș

english.text: In your patience you gained your reward, blessed Filofteia, enduring unceasingly in temptations, bearing blows, taking troubles gladly, showing mercy to the poor and filling the hungry; pray to Christ God, good virgin, that our souls may be saved.

death.note: The year the day line closes with for 7 декабря ст. ст., «(1060)». It is the first year of any kind this folder has carried: the Romanian and the Greek lines that made it gave none, and no life page stands behind this one to confirm it, so the basis is traditional and the year is this calendar's. Read 13 October 2026.
